behaviorChanges.change: A run with open steps exits non-zero
behaviorChanges.impact: A run that ends with planned steps still open reports stopReason "open_steps", ok:false and exit 1. It previously exited 0 as end_turn. Any benchmark adapter or script reading this envelope will score such runs differently — deliberately, and the older figures under docs/evidence/ stay as they are rather than being re-run.

behaviorChanges.change: filesChanged now includes apply_patch and worker-authored files
behaviorChanges.impact: One exported predicate (`filesChangedFrom` in lifecycle.ts) replaces four incompatible definitions across headless, the git auto-commit scope, the TUI transcript and the TUI footer. A headless envelope now lists files a worker wrote and files an apply_patch changed; both were invisible before.

behaviorChanges.change: A resumed run inherits the turns and second winds the killed one spent
behaviorChanges.impact: Only after a real crash (no session_ended marker) with open steps. A user who kills and resumes no longer gets a fresh 80-turn ceiling. A run that ended at a ceiling, or that the user aborted, still hands nothing forward.

behaviorChanges.change: A crash-resumed CHILD inherits its turn ceiling; a follow-up on a finished child does not
behaviorChanges.impact: The same rule one level down, split by how the child ended. A crash-resume gets max - used (floor: one turn); a follow-up on a child that reported gets a fresh ceiling. The cost and wall-clock caps carry in both cases, so a child resumed five times no longer gets five cost caps. The checkpoint gains a `status` field, written on the final save only, which is what distinguishes the two.

behaviorChanges.change: Checkpoints changed shape, rotate to two versions, and there is a prune command
behaviorChanges.impact: RunState no longer carries `messages`; the run id is <session>#<n>; at most two versions per run survive. Existing rows are untouched — `rune doctor` reports them (428 rows / 106 MB reclaimable on the founder's database) and `rune doctor prune-checkpoints --apply` removes them. Dry run by default, and no automatic purge anywhere.

behaviorChanges.change: The resume lease survives a crash, with a 30-minute TTL and a pid check
behaviorChanges.impact: Two PROCESSES can no longer resume one task_id at once. The pid check is the primary reaper and is instant — a crashed holder's lease is ignored the moment another process looks — and the 30-minute TTL only backstops a pid that tells us nothing. The refusal names the holder's pid, how long it has held, and that it clears when that process exits.

behaviorChanges.change: Dead workers' checkouts are reaped at engine start, and their work is COMMITTED to their own branch first
behaviorChanges.impact: A `.rune/worktrees/*` directory whose owning pid is dead is removed — but only after `git add -A && git commit --no-verify` onto that worker's own `rune/worker-*` branch, and only if that commit succeeds. No path deletes a branch. A checkout with no owner record (an older Rune's, a concurrent instance's) is never touched. Worker ids also change shape: `w1` becomes `w<8-char session prefix>-<n>`, which is the fleet-panel label and the branch name.

behaviorChanges.change: A compaction the eviction tier rescued now says its summarizer failed
behaviorChanges.impact: A `compaction` event can carry `failureReason` without `failed`. The transcript row reads "compacted without a summary" with the reason in the receipt instead of an ordinary "compacted" line; the persisted `auto_compaction` row gains `summaryFailure`; replay reconstructs it from either name. `failed` still means the compaction did not happen and still routes to a `compaction_failed` row.

behaviorChanges.change: Tool children die with the engine
behaviorChanges.impact: A SIGKILLed engine's `rune-tools` and its command's whole process group are gone within about 250 ms, where they used to survive indefinitely (measured 6 s and 13 s). Three layers: a getppid() watchdog in rune-tools exiting 129, process groups on the two sandbox backends that lacked them, and a pid ledger at `<workspace>/.rune/tool-children.jsonl` that a restarting engine reaps. A new gitignored file appears in every workspace that runs a tool.

behaviorChanges.change: One new event type on the wire and three new session row types
behaviorChanges.impact: `lifecycle` joins AGENT_TURN_EVENT_TYPES (and so every guarded reducer); `brief`, `compaction_failed`, `delegation_checkpoint` and `delegation_lease` join the session log. All additive; older clients ignore them. `run_trace` also now persists `turn_complete`, so a restarted process can report how the previous run ended.

behaviorChanges.change: provider_lost and stalled are unfinished verdicts on both surfaces
behaviorChanges.impact: Two stall paths that emitted no terminal event now emit exactly one `turn_complete`, and `provider_lost`, `open_steps` and `stalled` all reach UNFINISHED_STOP and the TUI's stoppedEarly latch. The TUI also stops treating a RECOVERED error as a run failure.

behaviorChanges.change: Mid-run steering is stored at full length
behaviorChanges.impact: The spine's `directive` cap went from 200 characters to GOAL_CAP (24,000). The injected block keeps its 200-character render cap, so nothing looks different; what changed is what a restart can read back.

behaviorChanges.change: A worker that ran tools but wrote nothing now succeeds
behaviorChanges.impact: It comes back with an INCOMPLETE report, a stop-reason line and its receipts instead of `success:false` with everything discarded. Machine consumers counting toolErrors will see fewer worker failures and more INCOMPLETE worker reports. A complete report is byte-identical to before.

behaviorChanges.change: A conflicted worker merge stays success:true but stops being invisible
behaviorChanges.impact: `integration` and `conflicts[]` reach `structured` and the lifecycle event's `children[]`, so a conflicted merge is a typed field rather than only `[MERGE CONFLICTS — …]` prose. The work is retained, not lost, which is why success stays true.

behaviorChanges.change: A criterion whose evidence was taken against a different revision drops one rung
behaviorChanges.impact: `CheckRecord` and `Evidence` now carry the workspace head and dirty flag, and a rung claimed against a different HEAD (or on a clean tree when the tree is now dirty) is demoted, with a notice naming which criteria moved.

behaviorChanges.change: rune doctor has a new section and a new subcommand
behaviorChanges.impact: `checkpoints:` in the report, and `rune doctor prune-checkpoints [--apply] [--keep N]`, dry run by default. As of b1b1262 the advisory's number is the number the command removes; before that the advisory over-promised (552/136 MB vs 428/106 MB).
